title: Minimum Spanning Trees: Kruskal and Prim

questions.prompt: What does a minimum spanning tree minimize?

options.text: The total weight of edges needed to connect all vertices
The distance between a chosen source and every other vertex
The number of vertices in the graph

questions.explanation: An MST connects all vertices with the least total edge weight (V-1 edges, no cycles). Minimizing per-source distances is the shortest-path problem instead.

questions.prompt: Which data structure does Kruskal's algorithm use to detect cycles efficiently?
questions.explanation: Union-find tells Kruskal in near-constant time whether an edge's endpoints are already connected (which would create a cycle).

questions.prompt: Which statements about MST algorithms are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: An MST of a connected graph has exactly V-1 edges
Kruskal sorts edges by weight and uses union-find
Prim grows a single tree using a min-heap
An MST is identical to the shortest paths from a source vertex

questions.explanation: An MST has V-1 edges; Kruskal is edge-sorting + union-find; Prim is heap-based tree growth. An MST is NOT the same as shortest paths.

questions.prompt: The ______ property states that the minimum-weight edge crossing any partition of the vertices belongs to some MST. (one word)
questions.explanation: The cut property is the greedy justification behind both Kruskal and Prim.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of Kruskal's algorithm.

items.text: Consider edges from lightest to heaviest
Add an edge only if it connects two different components
Stop once V-1 edges have been added

questions.explanation: Kruskal sorts edges, then greedily adds the lightest edges that don't form a cycle until the tree has V-1 edges.

questions.prompt: Match each item with its description.

pairs.right: Grow one tree with a min-heap
Lightest crossing edge is in an MST
V-1 edges, connects all, no cycle

questions.explanation: The two greedy algorithms apply the cut property differently to build a spanning tree of minimum total weight.
